texts.facts: Besides accident survivors often live poor quality of life and have to live with pain and suffering which are difficult to estimate. The case in hand also tells somewhat similar sordid story of road traffic accident victim(s). 2. The facts of the case in brief, as borne out from the record are that on 27.02.2019, one Mohd. Hasim, S/o Shri Majid Ahmad alongwith his two female colleagues namely Ms.Dolly, D/o Shri Parmod and Ms.Sushma, D/o Shri Som Prakash were going to their homes on motorcycle (make Bajaj Discover) bearing MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur registration No.DL-3SCE-8853 from Okhla Industrial Area after finishing their shift/work. The said motorcycle at the relevant time was being driven by Shri Mohd. Hasim while Ms.Dolly and Ms.Sushma were sitting as pillion riders thereupon. At about 10.30 AM, when they reached at Om Dharam Kanta, Khera Kalan Road, Delhi, they found the traffic lying stopped/stationary on the said road. Shri Mohd. Hasim accordingly stopped his motorcycle and waited for the traffic to start. In the meantime, one LPT truck (make TATA) bearing registration No.HR- 63B-2366 (offending vehicle), being driven by its driver at a very high speed as also in a rash and negligent manner hit the aforesaid stationary motorcycle from behind, as a result of which all the three motorcycle riders fell down on the road and sustained injuries. Seeing the condition of injured persons, the driver of offending vehicle got frightened and fled from the spot. A huge crowd gathered at the spot and somebody from the public made a call at number 100. PCR van arrived at the spot of accident and removed all the three injured persons to Satyawadi Raja Harishchandra Hospital, Narela (in short "SRHC Hospital"), where they were examined and opined to have sustained grievous injuries. Injured Mohd. Hasim was examined vide MLC No.899/2019; injured Ms.Dolly was examined vide MLC No.900/2019 and inured Ms.Sushma was examined vide MLC No.905/2019, all dated 27.02.2019. Owing to the grievous injuries suffered by Mohd. Hasim, he was Macp No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim vs Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: Fir ... on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135558726/ 2 immediately referred to higher centre, i.e Hindu Rao Hospital, Delhi for further treatment, where he remained lying admitted for a significant period of time and his case/final diagnosis was opined to be "open communited fracture tibia (left) Grade III-B". In the process, he also got himself medically treated from St.Stephen's Hospital, Delhi. 3. After nine days of the accident in question, FIR No.91/2019, dated 08.03.2019, U/s 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Alipur with regard to the said MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur accident. The police went about doing its job. During the course of investigation, respondent No.1/Dharmender Kumar was found to be the driver of offending vehicle, while respondent No.2/Dilip Kumar Jha was found to be registered owner thereof. It further came to fore during the course of investigation that at the relevant time, i.e on the date and time of accident, the offending vehicle was lying insured with respondent No.3/M/s The New India Assurance Company Limited (in short "insurance company"). The police investigated the matter and filed Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred to as "DAR"), which vide order dated 29.07.2019 was treated as a claim petition under 166 (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short "MV Act"). 4. It has been the case of petitioner/injured Mohd. Hasim that on the date of accident, he was aged about 23 years, graduate (having done Bachelor of Arts from Delhi University), doing private job by working as a "Field Executive" and earning about Rs.25,000/- per month. The accident in question took place due to sole negligence of respondent No.1 as a result of which he has suffered 38% permanent disability in his left lower limb; he could not do any work/job for about three years; he had to spend considerable amount on his medical treatment, conveyance, special diet, attendant charges; his marriage prospects has also been adversely affected on account of the permanent disability suffered by him and as such, he has prayed for compensation/claim @ Rs.34,05,754/- alongwith requisite interest quotient (as per Form XIV submitted on his behalf during the course of final arguments). 5. Despite being duly served, respondents No.1 and 2 did not file any reply/written statement in the matter. Accordingly, vide order dated 15.10.2019, their right to file written statement was closed and defence stood struck off. MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur 6. As regards the reply/written statement of respondent No.3/insurance company in the matter is concerned, it is again noteworthy that it filed "legal offer/Form-III", thereby offering a compensation amount of Rs.39,462/- (Rupees Thirty Nine Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Two Only) plus reimbursement of actual/ verified medical bills, to the petitioner/injured for the injuries suffered by him in the accident. The insurance company also raised the plea of "contributory negligence" by stating that accident in question had taken place due to the "contributory negligence" on the part of motorcycle riders as three grown up adults were "triple- riding" a two-wheeler/motorcycle in total contravention of the traffic rules and Macp No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim vs Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: Fir ... on 10 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135558726/ 3 regulations. Thus, the aforesaid compensation/claim amount was offered after deducting 50% towards "contributory negligence" on the part of motorcycle riders. 7. Before proceeding further, it is pertinent to mention here that the parties did try for an amicable settlement in the matter. The matter was even referred to Lok Adalat vide order dated 16.09.2019, however, unfortunately no amicable settlement could be arrived at between the parties. Second: "How to compensate the petitioner/injured". From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed in the matter vide order dated 15.10.2019. OPP. (3) Relief. 9. (i) In support of his claim, petitioner/injured Mohd. Hasim examined himself as PW-1 and Dr.Vivek Kumar Pathak, Specialist Orthopaedic from Maharishi Valimiki Hospital, Pooth Khurd, Delhi as PW-2 in the matter. Thereafter, PE in the matter was closed vide order dated 24.01.2023. (ii) On the other hand, despite being granted due opportunities, neither of the respondents led any evidence in the matter. Accordingly, RE in the matter was also closed vide order dated 28.02.2023. (ii) PW-1/Petitioner has proved on record the expenses incurred by him on his medical treatment through bills Ex.PW1/5 (Colly). He has also filed on record computation chart/list of medical bills (being part of Ex.PW1/5 Colly) reflecting the expenses incurred by him on his medical treatment, total amounting to Rs.31,946/- which is in consonance with the medical bills/prescriptions proved on record by him as Ex.PW1/5 (Colly).
texts.arguments: (i) The learned counsel for insurance company made a strong pitch that admittedly petitioner/injured/PW-1 alongwith his two female colleagues was triple riding a two-wheeler/motorcycle in total disregard/contravention of the traffic rules and in the process he/PW-1 could not control the same and got disbalanced. As such, it has been contended that contributory negligence @ 50% should be taken on the part of petitioner/injured. (ii) In the second limb of his submissions, it is very vehemently argued that in order to lend support to his case for proving the rashness and negligence on the part of respondent No.1, it was incumbent upon PW-1/injured to have examined his two female colleagues as well, but he has deliberately not examined them so as to avoid contradictions in their testimonies and as such, the story propounded by PW-1 is not liable to be believed. While saying MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur so, I am fortified by the observations made by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as "Ravi V/s Badri Narayan & Ors.", Civil Appeal No. 1926/2011, decided on 18.02.2011. In case of "Kaushnamma Begum and others V/s New India Assurance Company Limited" reported as, (2001) 2 SCC 9, it was inter alia held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that the issue of wrongful act or omission on the part of the driver of the motor vehicle involved in the accident has been left to a secondary importance and mere use or involvement of motor vehicle in causing bodily injury or death to a human being or damage to property would make the petition maintainable under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act. 19. (i) It may also be mentioned here that the standard of proof of negligence as required in a claim petition u/s 166 M.V Act is on the touchstone of preponderance of probability, as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation [(2009) 13 SCC 530]". (ii) The Hon'ble Gauhati High Court in case reported as, "[2012 (4) GLT MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur 516]", titled as, "Godavari Devi Sharma and Ors/ V/s United India Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors." It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly. 22. To assess compensation in personal injury cases arising out of rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle while awarding compensation the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case "Sanjay Kumar V/s Ashok Kumar & Anr.", reported as "(2014) 5 SCC 330" held the heads under which compensation is awarded, as follows:- Pecuniary damages (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:- (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non pecuniary damages (General damage) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). Furthermore, in "Civil Appeal No.7603/2012", titled as, "K. Suresh V/s New India Assurance Company Ltd. and Anr." (DOD: 19.10.2012), the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has been pleased to observe as under: Macp No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim vs Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: Fir ... Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the matter titled as " Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors." passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under:- " It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident. For this purpose, the Claims Tribunal and the MACP No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim V/s Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: FIR No.91/2019: PS Alipur Courts normally consider the nature of injury; the part of the body where the injuries were sustained, surgeries, if any, underwent by the victim, confinement in the hospital and the duration of treatment". 30. Keeping in view the seriousness of the injuries suffered by the petitioner/injured in the accident and the mandate of Hon'ble Supreme Court, as observed in case of "Ankur Kapoor V/s Oriental Insurance Company Limited" [2017 XI AD (SC) 485], I award a notional sum of Rs.80,000/- (Rupees Eighty Thousand Only) towards loss of general amenities and enjoyment of life to the petitioner/PW-1. Macp No.4202019: Mohd. Hasim vs Dharmender Kumar & Ors.: In case reported as, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, titled as, "DTC V/s Lalit", Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has been pleased to hold that victim is entitled to compensation even if no attendant is hired as some family member renders gratuitous services. (iii) Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company has very vehemently argued that on account of the injuries suffered by PW-1, his disability may be taken as in relation to the whole body. Hence, the appropriate multiplier would be "18" in view of judgment passed in case titled as "Sarla Verma Vs. DTC", 2009 ACJ 1298 SC. (Reliance placed on judgment "Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Sangeeta Devi & Ors bearing MAC. APP. 165/2011 decided on 22.02.2016).
